facts.sin: Sin means an act or thought that goes against God's will.
facts.god: God is the supreme being worshipped as creator and ruler of all.
facts.son: Son refers to Jesus Christ, called the Son of God.
facts.ark: The ark was the boat Noah built to survive the great flood.
facts.pew: A pew is a long bench where worshippers sit in church.
facts.joy: Joy is a deep gladness that comes from faith in God.
facts.law: The Law refers to the commandments given to Moses by God.
facts.nun: A nun is a woman devoted to religious life in a convent.
facts.pray: To pray is to speak with God in worship or request.
facts.holy: Holy describes something set apart and dedicated to God.
facts.hymn: A hymn is a song of praise sung in worship.
facts.amen: Amen is a word said at the end of a prayer meaning 'so be it'.
facts.alms: Alms are gifts of money or goods given to help the poor.
facts.halo: A halo is a circle of light shown around a holy figure in art.
facts.abba: Abba is an Aramaic word meaning 'father,' used to address God.
facts.font: A font is the basin used to hold water for baptism.
facts.mass: Mass is the Catholic service of worship centered on communion.
facts.monk: A monk is a man who lives a devoted religious life in a monastery.
facts.soul: The soul is the spiritual part of a person believed to live on.
facts.fast: To fast means to go without food as an act of devotion.
facts.tomb: The tomb is where Jesus was buried before his resurrection.
facts.faith: Faith means trust and belief in God.
facts.grace: Grace means God's freely given love and favor.
facts.mercy: Mercy means compassion and forgiveness shown to those in need.
facts.bible: The Bible is the sacred scripture of the Christian faith.
facts.cross: The cross is the symbol of Jesus' crucifixion and Christianity.
facts.angel: An angel is a heavenly messenger who serves God.
facts.altar: An altar is a table used for worship and communion in church.
facts.psalm: A psalm is a sacred song or poem, many found in the book of Psalms.
facts.glory: Glory means great honor and praise given to God.
facts.satan: Satan is the name for the devil, the enemy of God in scripture.
facts.devil: The devil is the spirit of evil opposed to God.
facts.creed: A creed is a statement summarizing core Christian beliefs.
facts.manna: Manna was the bread God provided for Israel in the wilderness.
facts.vicar: A vicar is a clergyman who leads a parish church.
facts.friar: A friar is a member of a religious order who preaches and serves.
facts.abbey: An abbey is a monastery led by an abbot or abbess.
facts.tithe: A tithe is a tenth of one's income given to support the church.
facts.saint: A saint is a person recognized for holiness and devotion to God.
facts.carol: A carol is a joyful song, especially sung at Christmas.
facts.gospel: The gospel is the good news of Jesus Christ's life and salvation.
facts.church: A church is a building or community where Christians worship.
facts.priest: A priest is a clergy member who leads worship and sacraments.
facts.prayer: Prayer is communication with God through words or thought.
facts.parish: A parish is a local church community and its area.
facts.deacon: A deacon is a church leader who assists in ministry and service.
facts.bishop: A bishop is a senior clergy member overseeing a group of churches.
facts.chapel: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship.
facts.heaven: Heaven is believed to be the eternal home of God and the faithful.
facts.spirit: The Spirit refers to the Holy Spirit, God's presence among believers.
facts.belief: Belief means holding something to be true, especially about God.
facts.sermon: A sermon is a talk given by a preacher to teach or inspire.
facts.cherub: A cherub is a type of angel often shown as a winged child.
facts.advent: Advent is the season of preparation before Christmas.
facts.easter: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
facts.repent: To repent means to turn away from sin toward God.
facts.rosary: A rosary is a string of beads used to count prayers.
facts.martyr: A martyr is a person who dies for their religious faith.
facts.pulpit: A pulpit is the raised stand where a preacher delivers a sermon.
facts.baptism: Baptism is a ritual of washing with water to mark new faith.
facts.worship: Worship means honoring and praising God.
facts.apostle: An apostle is one of the twelve disciples sent to spread Jesus' teaching.
facts.prophet: A prophet is a person who speaks messages from God.
facts.miracle: A miracle is an extraordinary event attributed to God's power.
facts.sabbath: The Sabbath is a holy day of rest and worship.
facts.messiah: The Messiah is the promised savior, identified by Christians as Jesus.
facts.penance: Penance is an act showing sorrow for sin and seeking forgiveness.
facts.convent: A convent is a community where nuns live and worship.
facts.steeple: A steeple is the tall tower on top of a church.
facts.chalice: A chalice is the cup used to hold wine during communion.
facts.trinity: The Trinity is the belief in God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
facts.incense: Incense is burned in worship as a symbol of prayer rising to God.
facts.pilgrim: A pilgrim is a person who travels to a sacred place for faith.
facts.vespers: Vespers is a service of evening prayer.
facts.diocese: A diocese is a district overseen by a bishop.
facts.epistle: An epistle is a letter, especially one written by an apostle.
facts.creator: The Creator refers to God as the maker of heaven and earth.
